headline: High: Cline’s default workspace write/network/MCP powers can conflict with a non-runnable docs-only repo, creating unsafe shared-workspace and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable tool surface and no shared channel is documented, so it cannot inject B directly. B can read/write workspace files and use MCP, so if A’s repo content is manually copied into B’s workspace, B could misread it as instructions. This is a limited, user-mediated bridge rather than a default channel.
conditions: IF A’s repository content is copied into B’s workspace or MCP context as plain text
IF B is configured to treat workspace text as instructions
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate folders
Do not paste A-generated text into B prompts
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Add a manual review step before B follows file content
Use read-only copies for any shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not a leakage source. B touches source code and browser screenshots and can write/read workspace files, so leakage is possible only if sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace. The pair does not show default sensitive-data exposure, but the shared filesystem path makes accidental disclosure plausible.
conditions: IF sensitive files are stored in the workspace shared with B
IF B is allowed to open or upload those files through its browser or model provider
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use a separate workspace for B
Redact screenshots before review
Restrict B to non-sensitive repos
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, while B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and shares state via filesystem across instances. The conflict is one-sided but still dangerous because B can overwrite or commit changes in a shared workspace without coordination. Uncertainty about A’s operational role does not reduce B’s default write risk.
conditions: IF A’s artifacts and B’s workspace point to the same directory
IF multiple B instances operate on the same git checkout without external locking
mitigations: Use one workspace per agent
Enable git locking or a single-writer policy
Stage changes in a separate branch
Pause extra B instances during edits
Snapshot the workspace before tool actions

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an informational repo, so its outputs can become reference material for B, which can then act with shell, browser, and git authority. Because B’s tool use is broad and approval-based rather than fully autonomous, the cascade exists in default workflows but is not guaranteed to become harmful without additional steps. The interaction is inferred from B’s action surface and A’s content role.
conditions: IF B uses A’s repository content as authoritative input
IF B executes shell, browser, or git actions based on unverified claims from A
mitigations: Require B to cite source lines before acting
Add a human verification checkpoint
Limit B to read-only analysis mode
Separate research from execution tasks
Log and review all tool-triggering prompts

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data class mismatch is documented for A, and B only lists source code and browser screenshots. Without a regulated data class or residency claim, there is no compliance pathway to assess. The absence of such fields is informative, so this remains non-applicable rather than merely uncertain.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI, EU PII, or financial records are introduced into the pair
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the workspace
Document data classification before use
Add a residency review for any new dataset
Use a separate compliant environment if regulated data appears
